rule: The tide bell is operated by a manual lever; it cannot ring without someone moving the lever.

chapters.memory: Lena remembered the winter when she had lived above the rope shop.
chapters.knows: Lena knew Tomas now held the brass key.
chapters.misbelieves: Ivo still believed Lena had the brass key, although he had watched the handover through the wrong window.
chapters.suspect: Lena could not tell whether the wet footprints belonged to Rook.
chapters.plan: Tomorrow, Lena intended to search every boat in the harbour.
chapters.hypothesis: If the fog lifted, the northern buoy might become visible.
chapters.dream: That night she dreamed the tide bell was ringing beneath the sea.
hooks: The register contained two entries for the same tide.
A blue thread protruded from the register’s stitched spine.
Rook wore a square impression of clean skin where his ring should have been.

relationship.anchor: Lena no longer trusted Tomas to interpret the archive without a witness.

chapters.believes: Tomas believed a public hearing would be safer than a private bargain.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Lena settled at the archive desk to wait for morning.

chapters.title: The Lever in the Rain

facts.subject: char:lena
facts.anchor: By midnight Lena was standing on the survey bridge.

facts.subject: item:brass_key
facts.anchor: Tomas handed the brass key to Ivo before entering the rain.

facts.subject: char:lena
facts.anchor: The clerk returned two coins, bringing Lena’s purse to seventeen.

facts.subject: char:rook
facts.anchor: Lena found Rook beneath the broken rail; he was dead.

facts.subject: char:ivo
facts.anchor: The sealed appointment proved that Ivo was the former municipal cartographer.

facts.subject: item:tide_register
facts.anchor: Lena took the tide register from Ivo and tucked it beneath her jacket.

facts.subject: char:tomas
facts.anchor: Tomas waited inside the town hall with the watch officer.

facts.subject: item:red_marker

claim: “I never drew that map,” Ivo said.
chapters.memory: Lena recalled stepping onto Merrow Quay during her first visit, one chapter of the inquiry earlier.
chapters.knows: Lena knew the bridge lever had been moved by a human hand.
chapters.misbelieves: Tomas believed Rook was still waiting in the hall, but the chair he remembered was empty.
chapters.suspect: Lena suspected the second tide entry concealed a meeting rather than a measurement.
chapters.plan: Lena planned to question the watch officer after sunrise.
chapters.hypothesis: If the second mark meant a meeting, someone else might have attended.
chapters.dream: She dreamed of Rook sitting dry and unhurt at the municipal desk.
hooks: The second tide entry matched the hour on the watch log.
The blue thread remained visible along the wet spine.
A crescent of green wax clung to the bridge lever.

relationship.anchor: Lena agreed to work with Tomas only while their notes remained open to the watch officer.

chapters.believes: Lena believed the watch officer would attend the hearing.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Lena stayed on the survey bridge beside the covered lever.

chapters.title: The Open Register

facts.subject: char:lena
facts.anchor: Lena entered the town hall before the hearing began.

facts.subject: item:brass_key
facts.anchor: Ivo returned the brass key to Lena in front of the watch officer.

facts.subject: char:lena
facts.anchor: She paid five coins for the sworn copy and kept twelve.

facts.subject: char:ivo
facts.anchor: The hearing clerk entered Ivo in the record as a municipal witness.

facts.subject: char:tomas
facts.anchor: Tomas returned to the archive to open it for the public.

facts.subject: item:red_marker

facts.subject: char:lena
facts.anchor: The nurse wrapped Lena’s bruised wrist in a clean bandage.

claim: Rook asked me to duplicate the entry.
“Rook asked me to duplicate the entry,” Ivo said.
chapters.memory: Lena remembered a summer apprenticeship whose starting date she could no longer place.
chapters.knows: Lena knew the duplicate entry had been made to conceal an unlawful docking fee.
chapters.misbelieves: Tomas had believed the blue thread was a repair, but the recovered note showed it was a page marker.
chapters.suspect: Lena could only guess who had left a boat moving beyond the fog.
chapters.plan: She intended to apply for a permanent survey post in the spring.
chapters.hypothesis: If the council published the fees, another hidden account might surface.
chapters.dream: In her last dream the two tides separated into ordinary lines of ink.
hooks: The duplicate entry concealed a second docking fee.
The blue thread marked the pocket holding the fee receipt.
Rook had pledged his ring to cover the missing fee.
The green wax came from the council’s receipt seal.

relationship.anchor: Lena trusted Tomas to keep the archive open under the new public rules.

chapters.believes: Tomas believed the published register would outlast their quarrel.
chapters.endStateAnchor: Lena remained in the town hall until the hearing record was sealed.

correctedCognition.content: Tomas knows the blue thread marked a pocket containing the fee receipt.

annotationPolicy.facts: Gold targets end-of-chapter state; explicit within-chapter before/change values remain arithmetic evidence. Do not create multiple active single-valued facts.
annotationPolicy.recalls: Unknown starts are null, not zero. Chapter-two memories explicitly dated to chapter one use [1,1].
annotationPolicy.claims: Keep reported dialogue separate from confirmed world facts.
annotationPolicy.traps: Plans, hypotheses and dreams produce no asserted world facts.
annotationPolicy.provisional: Uncertain sensory inference is provisional and never a confirmed premise.
